amendments.reason: Mirrored the scene across the centre line: negated every actor's x-coordinate and reflected each actor's facing (facing' = pi - facing, normalized to [0,2*pi)) so the whole picture now sits correctly in Navy's own defensive zone near x=-20 to -23. The q4 position-question reference point's x-coordinate was negated to match. Briefing: 'YOU is weak side' -> 'YOU are weak side'. q5 explanation: 'so YOU updates the coverage relationship' -> 'so YOU update the coverage relationship'.

questions.explanation: Possession was lost, so priority moves from attack to recovery; if Navy regains it, update.

options.text: An assumed empty passing lane for Gold 1

questions.explanation: Gold 1 carries while Gold 2 offers inside support, so recover middle and communicate; an empty-looking wall lane does not prove Gold 1 has no pass.

questions.prompt: Arrange one failed-pinch recovery.

options.text: Angle Gold 1 after middle is protected

questions.explanation: Turnover updates carrier; inside recovery protects net; once middle is covered, wall carrier can be angled.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an inside recovery lane that is below Gold 2 toward the Navy net.
questions.explanation: The target is below Gold 2 along the rink’s length and supports the direct route; angle Gold 1 only after the inside threat is checked.

questions.prompt: If Gold 2 receives before you arrive, what is your priority?

options.text: Contain Gold 2 as carrier and keep net-side lane closed

questions.explanation: The reception changes who can attack net, so switch scan and contain; if Gold 2 is covered, return to next threat.

questions.prompt: Why does the failed pinch change your first skating lane?
questions.explanation: Possession moved to Gold and inside support is closer to net, so middle recovery protects the highest-risk route; if Navy recovers, transition roles change.
